proposal.summary: Add one memory preventing follow-up extraction from discarding stronger existing evidence. Retain existing entries; the search signals were legitimate empty discoveries, and both fetch failures were recovered.

edits.title: Compare replacement cells with previously verified evidence
edits.content: A follow-up extraction can pass schema and verbatim-quote checks while silently dropping supported parts of an existing value. Before replacing a populated cell, supply its current value and supporting evidence alongside the new evidence, then compare the proposed replacement for lost attributes, qualifiers, or sources. A shorter statement in a navigation list or another person's page does not establish that omitted attributes are false. Preserve stronger person-specific evidence unless new evidence justifies a correction; investigate actual conflicts rather than blindly taking the latest extraction. Stage replacements until this comparison and quote checks pass. A failed corroborating fetch does not invalidate evidence already verified.

additional_candidates.description: Follow-up nationality extraction temporarily replaced a supported multi-country value with a narrower navigation-list value; the agent restored the stronger stored evidence.
Exact membership checks detected a reconstructed PDF quotation, followed by successful repair using a stored source slice.
Source review distinguished absent nationality evidence from extraction omissions and repaired incomplete affiliations.

decisions.reason: Reviewed all 34 occurrences. Signals 0–6 concern seven annual searches whose returned snippets contained no laureate names; inspection preceded the empty discovery records. Signals 7–31 concern nationality research for 25 already identified people, and signals 32–33 concern two further verification searches. These searches supplied useful evidence without discovering new entities. Entry 0 explicitly permits honest empty records for such cases. Its usage outcome therefore does not demonstrate recurrence of the premature-placeholder failure or justify changing it.

Both occurrences were isolated backend failures: Princeton returned HTTP 403, and TAP failed certificate verification. The first was resolved through a previously discovered alternative profile; the second left stronger previously fetched evidence available, ultimately restored. Neither URL was repeatedly retried or cited as successfully fetched. No host-specific prohibition or separate fetch-failure memory is warranted; the consequential replacement regression is handled separately.

The follow-up prompt omitted the existing person-specific evidence. Its output reduced a previously supported three-country nationality to one country from another person's page, and the mutation passed structure and quote checks. The next turn explicitly recognized the lost information and restored the original cell. This recovered failure exposes a semantic replacement check absent from the existing discovery, PDF-repair, and missing-field entries. Preserve that failure mode as a memory without storing the task's answer.

The initial affiliation quotation substituted text from the wrong interleaved PDF line. The agent located the actual passage, sliced the stored text, and rechecked membership; final citation checks passed. Entry 1 already captures this exact failure and complete repair procedure. Its recorded successful outcome supplies no evidence for revision or deletion.

Review established that the later annual releases lacked explicit nationality, prompting targeted alternative-source research rather than birthplace inference. Semantic audits also caught omitted affiliation locations and a former-role qualifier, which were repaired. Entry 2 already covers source absence, secondary institutions, and temporal qualifiers. Some audit suggestions expanded beyond announcement-listed affiliations, but the agent clarified scope and completed review; no additional edit is needed for this group.
